posts.author: FourthDimension
posts.body:
I am not sure if this is the right forum for product technical support or not.  Please move it if it isn't,
I bought a new laptop and have finally tried to install RPG Maker VX Ace and transfer my projects.  I installed it using a download that was saved when I initially bought the program.  It seemed to install perfectly and also installed the RTP.  But when I open the editor, it just displays the "loading" message in the grey rectangle for a few seconds before disappearing.
I have Googled compatibility with Windows 11 and the consensus I can see is that it has difficulty communicating with an Arm processor (whatever that is) like the Snapdragon that my PC is operating with.  I followed the suggestion of changing the emulation settings for the program but still nothing.
I don't really want to lose all the work I have put into my projects but I also don't want to keep running the old laptop that they are stored on so any help would be appreciated.  Thanks.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
the prozessor determines the lowest set og commands used in a computer.
VXA was programmed at a time when the Intel/AMD processors based on 8086 architecture were used in every PC.
In the last years other types of processor architecture were developed. Like ARM or others.
These have advantages, but they are NOT directly compatible.
you need an emulation that pretends to be an Intel Processor to run some programs

posts.author: FourthDimension
posts.body:
Thanks very much for this.
I am assuming that I am not the only person who has tried to transfer VXA onto a new computer since MS disbanded Windows 10 and come up against this problem.
Is there a download for such an emulator that anyone has used successfully?
Of course, it does render the question as to whether anyone could ever play a VXA game ever again if the engine is fundamentally incompatible on modern machines.  But I really don't want to get a newer version of RPGM and then have to start ALL over again.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
I think you don't really understand my answer above.
The Processor is a hardware difference, not a windows difference.
there are uncountable millions of computers using Win11 on an intel-processor and operating programs like VXA without any problem.
you only have problems because your computer has the wrong hardware and NOT because you use Win11
and even the latest maker (MZ) is still programmed and working with Intel processors, but most likely will not work on an ARM processor.
And there are dozens of different emulators, but I don't know which of them have variants that work with ARM-Architecture. I will probably never even purchase any computer with an ARM-Processor,
That part you'll have to research for yourself.

posts.body:
Never would have thought about it but Andar is right.

posts.author: FourthDimension
posts.body:
Thanks.  This is all very unfamiliar territory for me.  My first assumption when it didn't work was that it was because it wasn't compatible with windows 11.  I did... kinda... understand from my googling that it was the processor and the coding architecture that it wouldn't run with.  But then, the googling said that there were settings that would run it if they were changed and indeed another search says that there is a built-in emulator with no further download required.
I was just asking if anyone else has had this problem and can give me a quick fix before I start seriously messing around with my computer settings or downloading superfluous emulator programs that aren't necessary and aren't going to work.
It is reassuring to know that it doesn't require a newer engine though.  If I can get it fixed then I can keep running my familiar and much loved VXA.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
FourthDimension said:
says that there is a built-in emulator with no further download required.
Click to expand...
the build-in emulator focuses on getting programs written for Win 11/intel to run on Win11/ARM.
The older versions of Windows only have somewhat compatibility, with the older a program gets the less compatibility it has.
And VXA (or rather the critical display library) was basically programmed on WinXP, which is older than Win 7

posts.body:

posts.body:
Okay... this is really over my head.
Are you suggesting that if I were to purchase VX Ace through Steam, it would probably work because people who know what they are doing would ensure that it is compatible?  But that isn't guaranteed because you are basing that on an Intel processor and not an ARM processor.  But then even if that were to work, playing an RPG Maker game or even testing it would possibly not work anyway?
I honestly thought that this would be a relatively simple adjustment.  It's sounding like this is going to be the end for me.  It sounds like a huge operation involving skills way in advance of my own.

posts.author: DevRPG2k
posts.body:
FourthDimension said:
Are you suggesting that if I were to purchase VX Ace through Steam, it would probably work because people who know what they are doing would ensure that it is compatible?
Click to expand...
No, I meant that even running on a Windows with x86 architecture (x64 compatible with x32), VX didn't work due to something related to Windows 8, but it works on 10 and 11 (also x86).
It was an example of a type of incompatibility that occurred even though everything was in place for it to work.
What I said is that even if there was a way to use the editor, in the end the game probably wouldn't run.
Then I explained that the best solution is to change the engine, since MV and MZ can create games for Android, which is ARM, so it's possible to replace the NWjs (engine for Windows x86) with the one made for ARM:
Downloads
nwjs
nwjs.io
In summary, manually migrate your project to RMMV or RMMZ.

posts.author: FourthDimension
posts.body:
So I'm hearing that it is virtually impossible to get VXA to run on this computer without a serious amount of effort and technical knowledge.  There is no quick fix for it because the issue is fundamental to the core DNA of the machine architecture.
I could buy another machine with a different processor (not going to happen) or I could buy a different engine, emulate to get it working and lose all my current projects (also not going to happen).
I will need to keep running it on the same computer I was using, but given that the middle quarter of the keyboard doesn't work, that's not great.  But it's the best I can hope for.

posts.author: Roninator2
posts.body:
FourthDimension said:
manually migrate the project to MV or MZ. Is there an easy way to do that, or would it involve writing it all from the ground up?
Click to expand...
There is a script that you can run which will extract the database data and convert it to MV data.
Also the maps. but any scripts you were using will not be transferred. you have to find new plugins in MV. Also after that you would have to clean up the data as not everything is copied. Some values in MV do not exist in VX Ace. At least that's what I found when I tried to do that.
The conversion script was done by Shaz. Give a search and you should be able to find it.
I plan to move to MZ when my current project is done (if ever).

posts.author: kyonides
posts.body:
Well, there's no guarantee you necessary have to lose your projects in the process, yet, backing them up is completely normal. This being a processor issue, I doubt that purchasing MV or MZ will change anything. If they were built for Intel or AMD processors but not ARM ones, you'd still go through the same
hell
. So make sure they do support that architecture before you purchase anything.
